items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which historical event brought thousands of French words, such as 'court,' 'justice,' and 'beef,' into the English language?
options: The arrival of the Anglo-Saxons in Britain
The Norman Conquest of England in 1066
The invention of the printing press
The founding of the American colonies
items.explain: After 1066 the French-speaking Normans ruled England, so French vocabulary entered English, especially in law, government, and food.

concept.es: Cómo el francés normando influyó en el inglés

tip.en: Read a short timeline of the Norman Conquest and list French-origin words you already use every day.
tip.es: Lee una línea de tiempo de la conquista normanda y anota palabras de origen francés que ya usas a diario.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A student wants to find every verse in the Bible that contains the word 'shepherd.' Which reference tool is best for this task?
options: A thesaurus
An atlas
A concordance
An almanac
items.explain: A concordance lists each place a word appears in a text such as the Bible.

concept.es: Elegir la herramienta de consulta adecuada

tip.en: Practice matching tasks to tools: concordance for word searches, atlas for places, thesaurus for synonyms, encyclopedia for overviews.
tip.es: Practica emparejar tareas con herramientas: concordancia para buscar palabras, atlas para lugares, tesauro para sinónimos, enciclopedia para panoramas.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A student is writing a formal outline for an essay. Under main heading 'I. Causes of the Flood,' she has written only one subpoint, 'A. Heavy spring rains.' What rule of formal outlining should she follow?
options: Every subpoint A must be followed by at least a subpoint B.
Each main heading may have only one subpoint.
Subpoints should be written as complete paragraphs.
Main headings should use lowercase letters.
items.explain: In a formal outline, a heading is divided only if it has at least two parts, so an A requires a B.

tip.en: Remember that a subpoint needs a partner: outline an essay and check every A has a B.
tip.es: Recuerda que un subpunto necesita pareja: esquematiza un ensayo y verifica que cada A tenga su B.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
options: The deacons repaired the church roof last summer.
Our family will serve dinner at the shelter on Friday.
The volunteers have painted the classroom walls.
The new hymnals were donated by a local family.
items.explain: In 'were donated by a local family,' the subject receives the action, which is passive voice.

tip.en: Rewrite five sentences from active to passive and back, noticing who performs the action.
tip.es: Reescribe cinco oraciones de activa a pasiva y viceversa, fijándote en quién realiza la acción.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage.

After the storm drove their ship onto the rocks, the family stood on the empty shore with only a few barrels and tools. The father did not complain; he gathered his sons and asked each one to name something they could still be thankful for. The eldest pointed to the fresh spring nearby, the youngest to the goats that had swum ashore. By evening they had built a shelter from sailcloth and driftwood, and before sleeping they thanked God together for sparing their lives.

Which theme is best supported by the passage?
options: Wealth is the key to surviving hardship.
Gratitude and teamwork help people endure trials.
Nature is always cruel to those who travel.
Children should never be trusted with work.
items.explain: The family responds to disaster with thankfulness and shared work, which supports the theme of gratitude and cooperation.

concept.en: Finding the theme of a story
concept.es: Hallar el tema de un relato

tip.en: After reading a story, write one sentence about the lesson the characters' choices teach.
tip.es: Después de leer un relato, escribe una frase sobre la lección que enseñan las decisiones de los personajes.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Marcus stared at the empty bench where his grandfather used to sit. He wondered whether anyone else at church even noticed it was empty. The pastor smiled at him as he passed, but Marcus could not tell what the pastor was thinking.

From which point of view is the passage told?
options: First person
Second person
Third-person omniscient
Third-person limited
items.explain: The narrator uses 'he' and reveals only Marcus's thoughts, not the pastor's, which is third-person limited.

concept.es: Identificar el punto de vista narrativo

tip.en: Check the pronouns: practice labeling passages as first person, third limited, or third omniscient.
tip.es: Fíjate en los pronombres: practica clasificando pasajes como primera persona, tercera limitada u omnisciente.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which is the strongest thesis statement for an argumentative essay?
options: This essay is about school uniforms.
School uniforms have been around for a long time in many countries.
Schools should adopt uniforms because they reduce distractions, lower family costs, and build a sense of community.
Some people like school uniforms and some people do not like them.
items.explain: It takes a clear, arguable position and previews specific reasons.

tip.en: Turn a topic into a clear, arguable claim, then test whether someone could reasonably disagree.
tip.es: Convierte un tema en una afirmación clara y debatible, y comprueba si alguien podría razonablemente discrepar.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: My grandmother, who taught Sunday school for forty years, still remembers every student's name.
My grandmother who taught Sunday school for forty years, still remembers every student's name.
My grandmother, who taught Sunday school for forty years still remembers every student's name.
My grandmother who taught Sunday school, for forty years, still remembers every student's name.
items.explain: A nonrestrictive clause that adds extra information is set off by commas on both sides.

tip.en: Practice deciding if a clause is essential; if the sentence works without it, set it off with commas.
tip.es: Practica decidir si una cláusula es esencial; si la oración funciona sin ella, sepárala con comas.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales (late 1300s) is a famous example of literature written in which stage of the English language?
options: Old English
Middle English
Early Modern English
Present-Day English
items.explain: Chaucer wrote in Middle English, the form used roughly from 1100 to 1500.

tip.en: Make a simple chart of Old, Middle, and Modern English with a sample text for each.
tip.es: Haz un cuadro sencillo de inglés antiguo, medio y moderno con un texto de ejemplo de cada uno.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which part of a dictionary entry tells you that the word 'gospel' comes from the Old English 'godspel,' meaning 'good news'?
options: The pronunciation key
The part-of-speech label
The etymology
The usage note
items.explain: The etymology gives the origin and history of a word.

concept.es: Leer con atención las entradas del diccionario

tip.en: Look up three words and name each part of the entry, especially the etymology.
tip.es: Busca tres palabras y nombra cada parte de la entrada, sobre todo la etimología.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A test question says: 'Explain two reasons the early church grew rapidly in the first century.' Which sentence is the best way to begin an essay answer?
options: The early church grew rapidly in the first century for two main reasons: the bold preaching of the apostles and the love believers showed one another.
There are many interesting things to learn about history.
I think this is a good question, and I will try my best to answer it.
Rome was a large empire with many roads and cities.
items.explain: A strong essay answer restates the question and directly states the main points.

concept.es: Comenzar bien una respuesta de ensayo

tip.en: Practice starting by restating the question as a direct statement that previews your points.
tip.es: Practica empezar reformulando la pregunta como una afirmación directa que anticipe tus puntos.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood?
options: If I was the captain, I would change course.
The coach insisted that every player arrives on time.
If I were in your place, I would apologize to her.
I wish that it was Saturday already.
items.explain: The subjunctive uses 'were' for contrary-to-fact conditions: 'If I were in your place.'

tip.en: Write sentences with wishes and conditions, such as 'If I were...' and 'I suggest that he be...'.
tip.es: Escribe oraciones con deseos y condiciones, como 'If I were...' e 'I suggest that he be...'.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

Every family should set aside one evening a week for a shared meal without phones. Studies of teenagers suggest that regular family dinners are linked to better grades and stronger relationships. Moreover, a quiet table invites real conversation, prayer, and laughter. Surely an hour a week is a small price for such great rewards.

What kind of paragraph is this?
options: Narrative
Descriptive
Expository
Persuasive
items.explain: The writer argues for a position and urges readers to act, which makes it persuasive.

tip.en: Label paragraphs as narrative, descriptive, expository, or persuasive and note the clues that tell you.
tip.es: Clasifica párrafos como narrativos, descriptivos, expositivos o persuasivos y anota las pistas que lo indican.

items.subject: ela
items.skill: purpose of note and source cards
items.prompt: When researching, a student writes the number '3' at the top of several note cards. What is the main purpose of that number?
options: It shows how many quotations are on the card.
It links each note to the matching source card so the source can be cited.
It ranks the note by how important it is.
It tells which page of the final paper the note will go on.
items.explain: The source number connects each note to its source card, which holds the full citation information.

tip.en: Number each source card, then mark every note card with its source number to track references.
tip.es: Numera cada ficha de fuente y marca cada ficha de notas con ese número para rastrear las referencias.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage from a missionary's memoir (an original text).

For months I tried to explain the word 'forgive' to the villagers, but no word in their language seemed to fit. One afternoon an old man returned a goat that his neighbor had stolen years before. 'Why?' I asked. He answered, 'I have untied his debt from his neck.' That evening I wrote those words into my translation, and for the first time the people understood the gospel I had come to share.

What can the reader infer from the passage?
options: The author learned the meaning of the villagers' expression from an everyday act of mercy.
The author decided to stop translating and return home.
The old man was angry that his goat had been stolen.
The villagers already had a written Bible in their language.
items.explain: The author found the right phrase for 'forgive' by watching the old man's merciful act.

concept.es: Inferir el significado en una memoria

tip.en: Underline clues in the text and ask what the author implies but never says directly.
tip.es: Subraya pistas en el texto y pregúntate qué insinúa el autor sin decirlo directamente.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence follows the pattern Subject - Verb - Indirect Object - Direct Object (S-V-IO-DO)?
options: The choir sang beautifully.
Elena is the youth leader.
Grandpa gave my sister his old Bible.
The students elected Daniel president.
items.explain: 'Grandpa (S) gave (V) my sister (IO) his old Bible (DO).'

tip.en: Diagram sentences with indirect objects, asking 'to whom or for whom?' after the verb.
tip.es: Analiza oraciones con complemento indirecto, preguntando 'to whom or for whom?' después del verbo.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A reporter writes a news article in the 'inverted pyramid' style. Where should the most important facts (who, what, when, where) appear?
options: In the headline only
In the lead, at the very beginning of the article
In the middle paragraphs
In the final paragraph
items.explain: The inverted pyramid places the most important information in the lead and less important details later.

tip.en: Read a news story and notice how the key facts of who, what, when, where, and why come first.
tip.es: Lee una noticia y observa cómo los datos clave (quién, qué, cuándo, dónde, por qué) aparecen primero.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A student is writing a letter of application for a summer job but does not know the manager's name. Which salutation is correct for this business letter?
options: Hey there,
Dear Friend,
To whom it may concern;
Dear Hiring Manager:
items.explain: A business letter uses a formal salutation followed by a colon.

tip.en: Draft a job application letter, choosing a proper greeting when you don't know the recipient's name.
tip.es: Redacta una carta de solicitud de empleo, eligiendo un saludo adecuado cuando no conoces el nombre del destinatario.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In a library that uses the Dewey Decimal System, in which number range would you look for a book about the history of Christianity?
items.explain: The 200s are the Dewey class for religion.

concept.es: Ubicar libros con el sistema Dewey

tip.en: Visit a library and match the ten Dewey classes to the shelves where you find them.
tip.es: Visita una biblioteca y relaciona las diez clases Dewey con los estantes donde las encuentras.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A poem has fourteen lines written in iambic pentameter, three quatrains, and a final rhyming couplet. What form is it?
options: Shakespearean sonnet
Haiku
Limerick
Free verse
items.explain: Fourteen lines of iambic pentameter arranged as three quatrains and a couplet define the Shakespearean (English) sonnet.

tip.en: Compare sonnets, ballads, and haiku, counting lines, rhyme scheme, and meter in each.
tip.es: Compara sonetos, baladas y haikus, contando versos, esquema de rima y métrica en cada uno.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

(1) Honeybees communicate through a remarkable 'waggle dance.' (2) When a bee finds flowers, it returns to the hive and moves in a figure-eight pattern. (3) The angle of the dance shows the direction of the food compared to the sun. (4) Honey has been used as a sweetener for thousands of years. (5) The length of the waggle tells other bees how far away the flowers are.

Which sentence should be removed to improve the unity of the paragraph?
options: Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
Sentence 5
items.explain: Sentence 4 is about honey's history, not how bees communicate, so it breaks the paragraph's unity.

tip.en: Reread your paragraph and cross out any sentence that doesn't support the main idea.
tip.es: Relee tu párrafo y tacha cualquier oración que no apoye la idea principal.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence most likely comes from an autobiography rather than a biography?
options: She was born in a small farming town in 1921.
Historians agree that his early years shaped his later work.
I still remember the morning my father first took me fishing.
After the war, he moved his family to Chicago.
items.explain: An autobiography is written by the subject about himself or herself, usually in first person.

tip.en: Look for first-person clues like 'I' and personal memories to tell who is writing.
tip.es: Busca pistas en primera persona, como 'yo' y recuerdos personales, para saber quién escribe.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage (an original text).

For years Hannah refused to speak to the guard who had once mistreated her family. When she saw him at the market, old, thin, and alone, her first thought was to walk away. Instead, remembering the words 'Forgive, as you have been forgiven,' she bought him bread and sat with him while he ate. He wept, and she felt a weight lift from her own heart.

How does Hannah change in the passage?
options: She moves from bitterness to forgiveness.
She moves from trust to suspicion.
She moves from wealth to poverty.
She moves from courage to fear.
items.explain: Hannah begins by refusing to speak to the guard and ends by showing him kindness and feeling freed.

concept.es: Analizar el cambio de los personajes

tip.en: Track a character's actions at the beginning and end, then explain what caused the change.
tip.es: Compara las acciones de un personaje al inicio y al final, y explica qué causó el cambio.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence contains a predicate nominative?
options: The garden looks lovely in spring.
My uncle became a pastor last year.
The children carried the baskets home.
We gave the visitors a warm welcome.
items.explain: 'Pastor' follows the linking verb 'became' and renames the subject 'uncle,' so it is a predicate nominative.

tip.en: Find linking verbs and ask whether the word after them renames the subject.
tip.es: Busca los verbos copulativos y pregunta si la palabra que sigue renombra al sujeto.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which of the following is a sentence fragment?
options: The youth group packed boxes for the food bank.
Because the bridge had washed out during the night.
After lunch, we hiked to the top of the ridge.
Rain fell, and the river began to rise.
items.explain: It begins with a subordinating conjunction and has no independent clause, so it cannot stand alone.

tip.en: Check each sentence for a subject, a verb, and a complete thought; fix any that lack one.
tip.es: Comprueba que cada oración tenga sujeto, verbo y un pensamiento completo; corrige las que no.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which American literary movement of the mid-1800s, led by writers such as Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau, stressed intuition, self-reliance, and the spiritual value of nature?
options: Puritanism
Realism
Transcendentalism
Modernism
items.explain: Emerson and Thoreau were the leading Transcendentalists, who emphasized intuition, nature, and self-reliance.

tip.en: Read a short Emerson or Thoreau passage and discuss its ideas about nature and self-reliance.
tip.es: Lee un breve pasaje de Emerson o Thoreau y conversa sobre sus ideas acerca de la naturaleza y la autosuficiencia.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A speaker is persuading a city council to fund a new clinic. Which sentence relies mainly on ethos (the speaker's credibility)?
options: Imagine a mother holding a feverish child with nowhere to go at midnight.
The nearest emergency room is forty minutes away by car.
As a nurse who has served this community for twenty-two years, I have seen this need firsthand.
If we do nothing, more families will suffer every single year.
items.explain: The speaker builds credibility by citing professional experience, which is an appeal to ethos.

tip.en: Label persuasive sentences as appeals to logic, emotion, or credibility, and explain your choice.
tip.es: Clasifica oraciones persuasivas como apelaciones a la lógica, la emoción o la credibilidad, y explica tu elección.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage (an original text).

As the wagon rolled out of town, Jacob noticed that the left wheel wobbled slightly. 'It'll hold,' his brother said, waving the worry away. Jacob glanced at the steep mountain road ahead and said nothing, but he kept his eyes on that wheel for the rest of the morning.

What is the main effect of the detail about the wobbling wheel?
options: It describes the setting of the town in detail.
It foreshadows possible trouble on the journey ahead.
It reveals that the brothers dislike each other.
It shows the story is told in first person.
items.explain: The wobbling wheel and the steep road hint that a problem will happen later, which is foreshadowing.

concept.es: Detectar el presagio en un relato

tip.en: While reading, mark small details that hint at later events and predict what comes next.
tip.es: Mientras lees, marca detalles pequeños que anticipen hechos posteriores y predice lo que sigue.

items.subject: ela
items.skill: knowing what to cite in research
items.prompt: A student is writing a research paper on water shortages. Which of the following must be cited?
options: The fact that water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit
The student's own opinion in the conclusion
The fact that Florida is a state in the United States
A statistic from a 2023 government report on aquifer levels
items.explain: Specific data taken from a source must be cited; common knowledge and one's own ideas do not need citations.

concept.es: Saber qué citar en una investigación

tip.en: Practice separating common knowledge from specific facts, statistics, and ideas that need a citation.
tip.es: Practica distinguir el conocimiento común de los datos, estadísticas e ideas que necesitan cita.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the notice (an original document).

EMPLOYEE NOTICE: Shift-swap requests must be submitted to a supervisor at least 48 hours before the shift begins. Requests made with less notice will be approved only in a medical emergency. Both employees must sign the swap form. Approved swaps will be posted on the break-room schedule.

Lena wants to trade her Saturday 9:00 a.m. shift with a coworker. Based on the notice, what must she do?
options: Post the change on the break-room schedule herself by Saturday morning.
Text the supervisor on Friday night to explain the change.
Submit a form signed by both employees by Thursday 9:00 a.m.
Find a coworker and switch without telling anyone.
items.explain: The request needs both signatures and must be in at least 48 hours before the 9:00 a.m. Saturday shift, which is Thursday 9:00 a.m.

tip.en: Read real notices and underline deadlines, requirements, and who must act.
tip.es: Lee avisos reales y subraya plazos, requisitos y a quién le corresponde actuar.

items.subject: ela
items.skill: central conflict in In His Steps
items.prompt:
In Charles M. Sheldon's novel In His Steps (1896), members of a church pledge that for one year they will ask 'What would Jesus do?' before every decision and then act on the answer, whatever it costs them. A newspaper editor, for example, stops printing stories that he believes are harmful, even though he loses readers and money.

Which conflict is central to the novel, based on this description?
options: Characters struggle between following Christ's example and protecting their own comfort and success.
Characters struggle to survive a natural disaster in their town.
Characters compete with one another to win an election.
Characters try to solve a mystery about a stolen fortune.
items.explain: The pledge forces characters to choose Christlike actions even when it costs them money, status, or comfort.

concept.en: Central conflict in a classic novel
concept.es: Conflicto central en una novela clásica

tip.en: After each chapter, summarize the main choice characters face and what it costs them.
tip.es: Después de cada capítulo, resume la decisión principal que enfrentan los personajes y lo que les cuesta.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In John Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, a man named Christian travels from the City of Destruction to the Celestial City, meeting characters named Faithful, Hopeful, and Giant Despair. This kind of work, in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas, is called
options: a parody
an allegory
a satire
a biography
items.explain: An allegory is a story in which characters and events represent ideas, such as spiritual virtues and struggles.

tip.en: Match characters and places in a story to the ideas they symbolize.
tip.es: Relaciona personajes y lugares de un relato con las ideas que simbolizan.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Which option correctly fixes this comma splice?

'The storm knocked out the power, the family read by candlelight.'
options: The storm knocked out the power the family read by candlelight.
The storm knocked out the power, so the family read by candlelight.
The storm knocked out the power, and, the family read by candlelight.
The storm, knocked out the power, the family read by candlelight.
items.explain: Adding the coordinating conjunction 'so' after the comma correctly joins the two independent clauses.

concept.es: Corregir la coma que une oraciones

tip.en: Practice joining independent clauses with a semicolon, period, or comma plus conjunction.
tip.es: Practica unir cláusulas independientes con punto y coma, punto, o coma más conjunción.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: After the Civil War, writers such as Mark Twain and William Dean Howells tried to portray ordinary people and everyday life truthfully, using regional dialects and common settings. Which literary period does this describe?
options: Realism
Romanticism
Puritanism
The Harlem Renaissance
items.explain: Realism focused on accurate portrayals of ordinary life, and Twain and Howells are key Realists.

tip.en: Read a short Twain passage and note how it shows ordinary people and everyday speech.
tip.es: Lee un breve pasaje de Twain y observa cómo retrata a gente común y el habla cotidiana.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A student is writing a synthesis essay on whether teens should have part-time jobs. Source A says jobs teach responsibility. Source B says long work hours can lower grades. Which sentence best synthesizes the two sources?
options: Source A says jobs teach responsibility.
Many teenagers in America have jobs.
Source B is better than Source A because it uses more numbers.
While part-time work can build responsibility (Source A), limiting hours is important so grades do not suffer (Source B).
items.explain: Synthesis combines ideas from both sources into one connected claim.

tip.en: Compare two articles on one topic and write a paragraph blending their ideas with your own point.
tip.es: Compara dos artículos sobre un tema y escribe un párrafo que combine sus ideas con tu propio punto de vista.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the passage (an original text).

When the new girl dropped her tray in the cafeteria, the room went silent. Ruth set down her own lunch, knelt on the sticky floor, and began picking up the scattered grapes. 'Come sit with us,' she said quietly, handing the girl a napkin.

What does Ruth's behavior reveal about her character?
options: She is careless and clumsy.
She is shy and wants to be left alone.
She is compassionate and welcoming.
She is proud and wants attention.
items.explain: Ruth's actions, not direct statements, show kindness and a desire to include the new student.

tip.en: Notice what characters do, say, and how others react, then describe their personality from those clues.
tip.es: Observa lo que los personajes hacen, dicen y cómo reaccionan otros, y describe su personalidad a partir de esas pistas.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which work belongs to the Old English (Anglo-Saxon) period of British literature?
options: Beowulf
The Canterbury Tales
Paradise Lost
Pride and Prejudice
items.explain: Beowulf is the best-known Old English epic; the others are Middle English, Renaissance/Puritan, and Romantic-era works.

tip.en: Read a modern translation of Beowulf's opening and note its heroic themes and style.
tip.es: Lee una traducción moderna del inicio de Beowulf y observa sus temas heroicos y su estilo.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the sentence.

'When the reporter asked whether the team would quit, the coach's laconic reply was simply, "No."'

What does 'laconic' most nearly mean?
options: Angry and loud
Using very few words
Long and detailed
Uncertain and confused
items.explain: The one-word reply shows that 'laconic' means brief, using few words.

concept.es: Deducir el significado por el contexto

tip.en: Circle clue words near an unfamiliar word and guess its meaning before checking a dictionary.
tip.es: Encierra las palabras pista cerca de un término desconocido e intenta deducir su significado antes de consultar el diccionario.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

To replant a seedling, first water it well so the roots hold together. Next, dig a hole twice as wide as the pot. Then gently tip the seedling out, set it in the hole at the same depth, and press the soil firmly around it. Finally, water it again to remove air pockets.

Which mode of writing is this paragraph?
options: Narration
Description
Exposition
Persuasion
items.explain: The paragraph explains a process step by step, which is exposition.

tip.en: Sort passages into narration, description, exposition, or argument and explain the author's purpose.
tip.es: Clasifica pasajes en narración, descripción, exposición o argumentación y explica el propósito del autor.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence uses correct parallel structure?
options: She enjoys reading, to hike, and the piano.
She enjoys reading, hiking, and playing the piano.
She enjoys to read, hiking, and she plays the piano.
She enjoys reading, hikes, and to play the piano.
items.explain: All three items are gerunds: reading, hiking, playing.

tip.en: Check lists in your writing so every item uses the same grammatical form.
tip.es: Revisa las listas de tu escritura para que cada elemento use la misma forma gramatical.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: The words below have similar denotations. Which word has the most negative connotation?
options: Thrifty
Economical
Frugal
Stingy
items.explain: 'Stingy' suggests selfishness, while the other words suggest wise use of money.

tip.en: Compare synonym groups, such as thrifty and stingy, and explain the feeling each word carries.
tip.es: Compara grupos de sinónimos, como thrifty y stingy, y explica el matiz que cada palabra transmite.

items.subject: ela
items.skill: irony in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
items.prompt: In Samuel Taylor Coleridge's The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the becalmed sailors cry, 'Water, water, every where, / Nor any drop to drink.' What makes these lines ironic?
options: The sailors are about to reach a fresh-water spring.
The ship is sinking because it is full of rainwater.
The sailors refuse to drink because they are stubborn.
The sailors are surrounded by water yet dying of thirst because it is salt water.
items.explain: The situation is ironic: endless sea water surrounds them, but none of it can quench their thirst.

tip.en: Look for the gap between what is said and what is true, and discuss why the poet creates it.
tip.es: Busca la diferencia entre lo que se dice y lo que es cierto, y conversa sobre por qué el poeta la crea.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Early in Shakespeare's Macbeth, the witches chant, 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair.' Which theme of the play does this paradox introduce?
options: Appearances can be deceiving, and good and evil may be hard to tell apart.
True love always overcomes every obstacle.
Hard work is always rewarded with success.
Nature is peaceful and unaffected by human choices.
items.explain: The paradox signals that in the play things that look good may be evil, and the reverse.

concept.es: El tema en Macbeth de Shakespeare

tip.en: Rephrase memorable lines in plain words and connect them to the play's ideas about appearance and truth.
tip.es: Reformula frases memorables con tus palabras y relaciónalas con las ideas de la obra sobre apariencia y verdad.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: A student will give a speech using brief notes rather than reading a full script or memorizing every word. Which delivery method is this, and why is it often recommended?
options: Manuscript delivery, because it guarantees no mistakes
Impromptu delivery, because it needs no preparation
Memorized delivery, because it sounds the most natural
Extemporaneous delivery, because it is prepared yet allows eye contact and a natural tone
items.explain: Extemporaneous speaking uses prepared notes and a conversational style with eye contact.

tip.en: Rehearse aloud with a few key-word cards, working on eye contact, pace, and clear voice.
tip.es: Ensaya en voz alta con pocas tarjetas de palabras clave, cuidando el contacto visual, el ritmo y la claridad.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which British literary period, including poets such as William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge, emphasized emotion, imagination, and the beauty of nature?
options: The Restoration
The Romantic period
The Victorian period
The Modern period
items.explain: Wordsworth and Coleridge launched English Romanticism, which valued emotion, imagination, and nature.

tip.en: Read a short Wordsworth poem and note its focus on nature, emotion, and imagination.
tip.es: Lee un poema breve de Wordsworth y observa su enfoque en la naturaleza, la emoción y la imaginación.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Using word parts (circum- = around; loqu/locut = speak), what does 'circumlocution' most nearly mean?
options: Speaking clearly and directly
Traveling around the world
Talking around a subject instead of stating it plainly
Speaking in a loud, forceful voice
items.explain: Circum (around) + locution (speaking) = speaking around a point.

tip.en: Learn common Latin and Greek roots and combine them to work out unfamiliar words.
tip.es: Aprende raíces latinas y griegas comunes y combínalas para descifrar palabras desconocidas.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement is an example of an ad hominem fallacy?
options: We should not accept Mr. Lee's plan for the budget, because he dresses badly.
Two of my friends got sick after eating sushi, so all sushi is unsafe.
Either we cancel the trip or everyone will get hurt.
Everyone is buying this phone, so it must be the best one.
items.explain: Ad hominem attacks the person (his clothing) rather than his argument; the others are hasty generalization, false dilemma, and bandwagon.

tip.en: Collect examples of fallacies like ad hominem and explain why each one fails to prove a point.
tip.es: Reúne ejemplos de falacias como el ad hominem y explica por qué ninguna demuestra el argumento.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt:
Which revision of the sentence uses correct parallelism?

'The mission trip was not only exhausting but also it rewarded us.'
options: The mission trip not only was exhausting but also it was rewarding.
The mission trip was not only exhausting but also rewarding.
The mission trip was not only exhausting, it also rewarded us.
Not only the mission trip was exhausting but also rewarding.
items.explain: After 'not only' and 'but also,' both parts should be the same form: two adjectives, 'exhausting' and 'rewarding.'

tip.en: Make sure the words after 'not only' and 'but also' share the same grammatical form.
tip.es: Asegúrate de que lo que sigue a 'not only' y 'but also' tenga la misma forma gramatical.
